facts.title: Reclaimed water can help feed your lawn
facts.statement: Most reclaimed irrigation water carries nitrogen and phosphorus, so a lawn on reclaimed water may need less fertilizer.
lead: Most reclaimed irrigation water carries nitrogen and phosphorus, so a lawn on reclaimed water may need less fertilizer.
UF/IFAS says reclaimed water can supply part of the nitrogen and all of the phosphorus that turfgrass needs.
Nutrient levels vary by source, so your water provider can tell you what yours carries.
quotes: Depending on the level of treatment and storage, reclaimed water may contain significant amounts of nutrients. Plants in the landscape can use the nutrients present in reclaimed water, potentially reducing the need for applying fertilizer.

Using reclaimed water for irrigation can provide a portion of the nitrogen and all the phosphorus required by turfgrass (Menzel and Broomhall, 2006). Accounting for nutrients from reclaimed water in the nutrient budget can reduce nitrogen fertilizer applications, resulting in lower costs.

Most reclaimed water contains nutrients, such as nitrogen and phosphorus, that can contribute to the landscape's fertilization needs; therefore, fertilization could potentially be reduced to account for the extra nutrients in reclaimed water. Levels of nutrients vary according to the source, so check with your water provider for specifics.

facts.statement: Watering in the evening before dew forms, or in the morning after it dries, keeps grass wet longer; watering while dew is already on the grass lowers the risk of disease; dew is usually present in the predawn hours; water only on the days and at the times your city or county allows.

Never lose more than one-third of the blade at once.

facts.title: Why grass can yellow after a spring nitrogen feeding
facts.statement: Iron deficiency is common in Florida lawns in spring after a nitrogen feeding, and it usually fades within a few weeks.
lead: UF/IFAS says iron deficiency is common in Florida lawns in spring after a nitrogen feeding.
It shows up most in bahiagrass, centipedegrass and St. Augustinegrass, which can look yellow in spots just when you expect them to green up.
It usually fades within a few weeks.
quotes: Iron deficiency is commonly observed in Florida in the spring following N fertilizer applications, especially to bahiagrass, centipedegrass, and St. Augustinegrass. This can be frustrating because the N application should have resulted in greener turfgrass, but, in fact, the lawn may appear chlorotic in places.
Springtime occurrences of Fe deficiency normally dissipate within a few weeks.

facts.title: Too much nitrogen invites lawn fungus
facts.statement: Extra nitrogen invites brown patch and gray leaf spot; too little invites dollar spot. Nitrogen is easy to add and impossible to remove.
lead: UF/IFAS says too much nitrogen encourages brown patch and gray leaf spot, while very low nitrogen sets the stage for dollar spot.
That is why a lawn should get only the nitrogen its grass needs: it is easy to add nitrogen but impossible to remove it.
When large patch or gray leaf spot keeps coming back, too much water and nitrogen may be to blame.
quotes: For example, excessive nitrogen applications encourage brown patch and gray leaf spot diseases, while very low nitrogen levels are conducive for the development of dollar spot disease. The minimal amount of nitrogen required for the particular species of turfgrass in the lawn should be applied because it is easy to add nitrogen but impossible to remove it.
If large patch or gray leaf spot diseases are a continuous problem, excessive watering and nitrogen fertilization may be responsible.

facts.title: Large patch is a cool-season disease
facts.statement: Large patch is most likely to show up from November through May, when temperatures are below 80°F and the grass stays wet for 48 hours or more; the fungus does not affect roots.
lead: Large patch is most likely to show up from November through May, when temperatures are below 80°F and the grass stays wet for 48 hours or more.

The fungus does not affect the roots.
quotes: This disease is most likely to be observed from November through May when temperatures are below 80°F. It is normally not observed in the summer months. Infection is triggered by rainfall, excessive irrigation, or extended periods of high humidity resulting in the leaves being continuously wet for 48 hours or more.
Roots are not affected by this pathogen.
Excessive nitrogen application during potential disease development periods should be avoided.
It often becomes a problem in fall, when cooler temperatures and damp weather create ideal conditions for the fungus.

facts.title: A palm short on potassium needs its old fronds
facts.statement: Discolored older palm fronds are feeding the palm potassium; cutting them off makes the palm pull potassium from the green fronds above.
lead: When a palm is short on potassium, its older, discolored fronds keep feeding it potassium.
UF/IFAS says to leave those fronds on: if they are cut off, the palm pulls potassium from the green fronds above them.
Repeated pruning of those fronds can speed the decline of a badly deficient palm, even to its death.
quotes: If these older discolored leaves are removed, the palm then removes K from the next leaves up within the canopy that are currently green and symptom free. Repeated pruning of K-deficient older leaves has been shown to reduce the number of green, symptom-free leaves within the canopy (Broschat 1994) and, in severely K-deficient palms, is known to accelerate the rate of decline leading to death of the palm.
Despite their unattractive appearance, these leaves should be left on the palm as they are providing K in the absence of sufficient K in the soil.

facts.title: Palms stripped to a few fronds lost crowns more often
facts.statement: After the 2004-2005 hurricanes, UF saw that palms stripped to a few fronds lost their crowns more often than full palms.
lead: After the 2004-2005 hurricanes, UF saw that palms stripped to a few fronds lost their crowns more often than full palms.
In UF/IFAS's words, these "hurricane-cut" palms were more likely to have their crowns snapped off than those with fuller crowns.
quotes: However, observations of palms after the severe hurricane seasons of 2004 and 2005 in Florida showed that these "hurricane-cut" palms were more likely to have their crowns snapped off than those with fuller crowns (Figures 13 and 14).
facts.notes: high. (UF calls this an observation; the paper cites supporting oil-palm research.)

facts.title: High-nitrogen lawn fertilizer can kill a palm
facts.statement: The roots of large palms typically reach 50 feet or more from the trunk; high-nitrogen lawn fertilizer, even 30 feet away, has killed palms by triggering potassium deficiency.
lead: The roots of large palms typically reach 50 feet or more from the trunk.
They take up whatever fertilizer goes on the lawn around them.
High-nitrogen lawn fertilizer, even 30 feet away, has killed palms by triggering potassium deficiency.
quotes: Roots of large palms typically extend out 50 feet or more from the trunk in all directions and will take up whatever fertilizers have been applied to the turfgrass.
High N fertilizers applied to turfgrass, even 30 feet away from a palm on one side only, have been known to kill palms from induced K deficiency.

facts.title: Aedes mosquitoes stay close; black salt marsh mosquitoes travel
facts.statement: Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus fly only a few blocks in their lifetime, but the black salt marsh mosquito has a long flight range and emerges in large numbers after rains and flooding.

facts.title: One bug zapper, 10,000 insects, only 8 mosquitoes

facts.title: Drywood termites need no soil
facts.statement: Drywood termites live entirely inside wood and push out pellets that are hexagonal in cross section; after a treatment, a new and growing pile of pellets usually means it did not work.

the removal of all pellets and wings after a treatment provides a good monitoring system. After a treatment that has been accompanied by these removal measures, any new and growing piles of pellets and/or presence of alates or wings, typically indicate that the treatment was unsuccessful.

facts.title: Formosan termites can hollow a live tree
facts.statement: Formosan termites can hollow out a living tree's core, leaving a healthy-looking tree that can collapse in high winds.

facts.title: White-footed ant colonies can reach 3 million
facts.statement: White-footed ant colonies range from 8,000 to 3 million ants, and nearly half are egg-laying females; the best policy is to keep plants from touching outside walls.
lead: UF/IFAS says white-footed ant colonies range from 8,000 to 3 million ants.
Nearly half are egg-laying females.
UF/IFAS says the best policy is to keep plants from touching your outside walls.
quotes: Colony population estimates vary from 8,000 to 3 million individuals
Nearly half of the entire WFA colony is composed of fertile, reproductive females called intercastes
Laboratory tests (2002–2005) at the UF/IFAS Research and Education Center in Fort Lauderdale have shown baits to be the only effective management method to date for WFA control.
best policy is to not have any vegetation touching exterior walls.

facts.title: Florida carpenter ants do not nest in sound wood
facts.statement: Florida carpenter ants nest in voids and rotten wood, never sound wood; they bite but do not sting.
lead: UF/IFAS says Florida carpenter ants nest in existing voids or dig only into soft material, such as rotten wood or foam.
They will not dig nesting tunnels in sound wood.
They can bite, but they do not sting.
quotes: Florida carpenter ants seek either existing voids in which to nest or excavate only soft materials such as rotten or pithy wood and Styrofoam. Other concerns are that these ants sting (they do not) and bite (they do).
They will not excavate nesting galleries in sound wood.
Tall trees touching structures cause "bridges" which provide foraging access into buildings.

facts.title: Big "palmetto bugs" are mostly outdoor roaches
facts.statement: The big roaches Floridians call palmetto bugs are generally found outdoors and do not survive well indoors, so removing the roach is often all that is needed.
lead: The big roaches Floridians call palmetto bugs, the American, Australian, brown and smokybrown, are generally found outdoors.
UF/IFAS says outdoor cockroaches do not survive well indoors, and people often overreact when they see them.
Often, removing the roach from the house is all that is needed.
quotes: The larger cockroaches—American, Australian, brown, and the smokybrown—are 1–1/4 to 2 inches (31–51 mm) long and are often called palmetto bugs. Though they are generally found outdoors, they can become indoor problems when they migrate or are carried indoors.

Outdoor cockroaches do not survive well indoors, and many times people overreact to the presence of these cockroaches. Often, removal of these outdoor cockroaches from the house is all that is needed for control.
The Asian cockroach looks very much like a German cockroach, except it flies. Asian cockroaches live outside and are attracted to the lights from buildings.

facts.title: Cockroaches need water more than food
facts.statement: A German roach can survive only 12 days with food but no water, but about 42 days with water but no food; cockroaches often come indoors in a drought, looking for moisture.
lead: German cockroaches can survive only 12 days with food but no water.
However, if only water is present with no food, cockroaches can survive for about 42 days.
Cockroaches often come indoors during periods of drought because they are looking for moisture.
quotes: Water is the most important factor in cockroach survival. German cockroaches can survive only 12 days with food but no water. However, if only water is present with no food, cockroaches can survive for about 42 days. Cockroaches often come indoors during periods of drought because they are looking for moisture.

facts.title: German roaches ride in on grocery bags and breed in boxes
facts.statement: German roaches can ride in on infested grocery bags and breed in corrugated boxes, so check groceries and get rid of extra boxes fast.
lead: UF/IFAS says German cockroaches can get into a home in infested grocery bags.
They also breed in corrugated cardboard boxes.
UF/IFAS advises checking groceries before you put them away and getting rid of boxes you do not need right away.
quotes: German cockroaches can initially infest a structure when infested grocery bags are brought inside. Inspect groceries for cockroaches before storing. Keep grocery bags in outside storage areas.
Cockroaches breed prolifically in corrugated cardboard boxes. Discard unnecessary boxes immediately.
contact with these allergens can result in mild to severe rashes, other allergic reactions, and in extreme cases death from asthma attacks.

facts.title: Roof rats nest in old palm fronds and can jump to a house
facts.statement: Roof rats, Florida's top rodent pest, nest in old palm fronds and attics, and can jump eight feet from a tree to a house.
lead: UF/IFAS says roof rats are now the number one rodent pest in Florida.
They like to nest in attics, soffits, hollow trees and the old fronds on palm trees.
Rats have been known to jump eight feet from a tree to a house.
quotes: Did you realize that rats have been known to jump eight feet from a tree to a house?
Roof rats are now the number one rodent pest in Florida.
They also prefer to keep their nests in attics, soffits, hollow trees, and the old fronds on palm trees
Removal of old palm leaf skirts such as those found on Mexican fan palms (Figure 10) can remove hiding places for rats, snakes, scorpions, and other desirable or not so desirable wildlife.
When they invade buildings, they chew through wires that can potentially start fires, gnaw through plastic and lead water pipes, make holes in walls and cause other structural damage.
facts.notes: high (each piece is stated directly; the jump distance comes from a county blog, not a research paper).

facts.title: A mouse fits through a pencil-width hole
facts.statement: A mouse can squeeze through a hole the width of a pencil, so any gap you can fit a pencil into needs sealing.
lead: The CDC says mice can fit through a hole the width of a pencil.
UF/IFAS says rats can squeeze through cracks one-half of an inch wide.
quotes: Mice can fit through a hole the width of a pencil (1/4 inch or 6 millimeters in diameter).
rats can squeeze through cracks one-half of an inch wide

facts.title: Never sweep rodent droppings
facts.statement: Sweeping or vacuuming rodent droppings can put germs in the air; the CDC says to spray them with an EPA-registered disinfectant until very wet and let it soak as the label directs.
lead: The CDC says not to sweep or vacuum rodent urine, droppings or nesting material.
Diseases mainly spread from rodents to people when people breathe in contaminated air.
The CDC says to spray the droppings with an EPA-registered disinfectant until they are very wet, then let it soak as the label directs.
quotes: Don't vacuum or sweep rodent urine, droppings, or nesting materials.
Spray urine and droppings with bleach solution or an EPA-registered disinfectant until very wet. Let it soak for 5 minutes or according to instructions on the disinfectant label.
Diseases are mainly spread to people from rodents when they breathe in contaminated air.

facts.title: Brown recluses are not established here
facts.statement: Unconfirmed brown recluse spider bites are reported in Florida every year, but no brown recluse specimen has ever been collected in Tampa; the widow spiders are the only spiders native to or established in Florida with medically significant venom.
lead: Unconfirmed brown recluse spider bites are reported in Florida every year.
But UF/IFAS says no brown recluse specimen has ever been collected in Tampa.
UF/IFAS says the only spiders native to or established in Florida with medically significant venom are the widow spiders.
Widow spiders are shy and not aggressive, and bites rarely happen unless the spider is taunted or accidentally crushed.
quotes: The actual numbers are less important than the fact that a significant number of unconfirmed brown recluse spider bites are reported in the state every year. Yet not one specimen of brown recluse spider has ever been collected in Tampa, and the only records of Loxosceles species in the entire region are from Orlando and vicinity.
The only spiders native to or established in Florida with medically significant venom are the widow spiders (Latrodectus spp.).
widow spiders are shy and non-aggressive, and bites rarely occur unless the spider is taunted or accidentally crushed/pinched in clothing

facts.title: A crushed yellowjacket can call the colony
facts.statement: An injured yellowjacket often releases an alarm scent that sets off the colony, and unlike honeybees they can sting again and again.
lead: UF/IFAS says an injured yellowjacket or hornet often releases an alarm scent that quickly sets off an aggressive defense from the rest of the colony.
Unlike a honeybee, which dies after it stings, these wasps can sting as often as they find a target.
quotes: Unlike the honeybee, which dies upon inflicting a single sting, vespid wasps may sting as often as they find a target. In fact, when a yellowjacket or hornet is injured, it often releases an "alarm pheromone" which quickly results in an aggressive, defensive behavior from other members of the colony.
